guidebook.intro: Talk about plans, the weekend and your dreams. Runyankore has a near future with -za ku- and a later future with -ri-.

tips.title: Soon: ninza ku-
body: **-za** (go, come) + **ku-** + verb is the everyday future: **Ninza kugyenda** (I’m going to go), **Nituza kurya** (we’re going to eat), **Naaza kuija** (he’s going to come).

tips.title: Someday: -ri-
body: For plans further away or less certain, add **-ri-**: **Ndigyenda Kampala** (I will go to Kampala), **Ndigaruka** (I will come back), **Turibugana** (we’ll meet).
**Eizooba rimwe** is “one day”: **Eizooba rimwe ndigamba Orunyankore gye**.

culture.title: Ruhanga naayenda
body: Plans often end with **Ruhanga yaaba naayenda**, “if God wills”, like Inshallah in Swahili or Katonda bw’anaayagala in Luganda.
